text:
leah: Quick heads-up — just opened a docs PR to clarify burst credits across tiers, update metering examples, and add a unified SDK snippet for Node/Python. Could use a pricing SME and a devex review. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4215 @devex :eyes:
owen: Thanks. Link looks good. I'll check the pricing math tomorrow morning. Do we have currency examples for monthly vs pay-as-you-go?
maya: Pushed a Node & Python snippet to the PR. Node example uses the new `client.usage.getQuota()` helper. Snippet: ```js
const q = await client.usage.getQuota({customerId});
console.log(q.tier, q.burstRemaining);
```
sam: noticed one broken link in the pricing page to /console/usage — I can patch that in a follow-up. Also found we mention "per-1k token" in one spot and "per-token" in another; should standardize to "per-1k tokens" for the public examples.
leah: Good catch @sam. Standardizing to "per-1k tokens" makes the math easier for examples. Owen — when you do the pricing check, can you include an example converting USD/month reserved slots -> effective per-token price? That's what customers keep asking for.
owen: Yep. I'll add a small table: reserved capacity -> tokens/sec -> monthly cost -> effective cost/1k tokens. Also flagging that Dedicated customers have different metering: no token-level metering by default if they enable private billing. We should add a migration note.
maya: For the SDK snippet, do we want to show both streaming + non-streaming usage? Maybe keep streaming separate. Current PR has a short streaming example but it's not labeled clearly. I'll add headings.
leah: Please label clearly. Also add a callout for "quota headers" behavior on Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted (X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining, X-Redwood-Burst-Window). Sam — can you confirm header names from the runtime?
sam: Confirmed. Headers are `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining` and `X-Redwood-Burst-Window-Seconds`. For Dedicated with private billing the quota header is only present when metering is enabled. I'll add a short code sample showing how to read them in Node: ```js
const remaining = res.headers.get('x-redwood-quota-remaining');
const windowSec = res.headers.get('x-redwood-burst-window-seconds');
```
devex-bot: Preview site deployed: https://deploy-preview-4215--docs.redwood.ai (checks: linkscan passed, snippet-lint passed) :white_check_mark:
owen: Preview looks right. One nit: the dashboard screenshot uses the old metric `requests.count` instead of `tokens.ingested` — update to `tokens.ingested` for usage analytics panels.
maya: I'll update the screenshot and include the JSON for the Grafana panel in the PR so SEs can import it.
leah: Can someone add a short migration checklist for accounts moving from Hosted -> Dedicated? Key points: meter differences, header availability, reserved capacity pricing example, and how burst credits are applied. Keep it < 6 bullets.
sam: Added a checklist draft in the PR comments. Also added a tiny e2e test verifying the SDK snippet compiles (node 18).
owen: I've pushed the pricing table and the USD->per-1k-token calc. Also added a brief note about rounding assumptions (we round to 2 decimal places for customer-facing examples).
leah: Awesome. If no more blockers, I'll request final reviews and merge after CI. Thanks everyone! :tada:
